title: HTTP/2 CONNECT Tunneling for SSRF and Port Scanning

technique.summary: Abuse HTTP/2 CONNECT method to establish tunnels to internal services for port scanning and accessing internal network resources. H2 CONNECT creates a bidirectional byte stream that can tunnel arbitrary protocols including HTTP/1.1, enabling access to services that are otherwise unreachable from the external network. Use execute_command with curl --http2 as the execution path (not http_request).
steps: Confirm HTTP/2 support on target: check ALPN negotiation, h2 in Alt-Svc header, or response protocol
Send HTTP/2 CONNECT request to internal host:port — observe :status pseudo-header
:status 200 indicates port is open and tunnel established; 503/502 indicates closed or filtered
Port scan internal hosts: iterate through common ports (80, 443, 8080, 8443, 3306, 5432, 6379, 27017)
Once tunnel established to open port, push raw HTTP/1.1 requests through the tunnel
Access internal APIs, admin panels, or databases through the established tunnel
Use H2 multiplexing for concurrent port scans (multiple CONNECT streams simultaneously)

payloads.notes: H2 CONNECT probe — :status 200 = open, 503 = closed. Execute via execute_command, not http_request
Push HTTP/1.1 request through established H2 CONNECT tunnel to internal admin panel

payloads.payload: for port in 80 443 8080 8443 3306 5432 6379; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --http2 -X CONNECT --proxy https://target.com internal:$port; echo ":$port"; done
payloads.notes: Port scan loop via H2 CONNECT — execute via execute_command

payloads.payload: curl --http1.1 -H 'Upgrade: h2c' -H 'Connection: Upgrade, HTTP2-Settings' -H 'HTTP2-Settings: AAMAAABkAAQCAAAAAAIAAAAA' https://target.com/
payloads.notes: h2c upgrade attempt — cleartext HTTP/2 via Upgrade header when direct H2 is not available

bypassTechniques: h2c upgrade via Upgrade: h2c header when target doesn't advertise HTTP/2 but backend supports it
Use hostname instead of IP address for internal targets to bypass IP-based allowlists
WebSocket upgrade as alternative tunnel: Upgrade: websocket can establish similar bidirectional streams
H2 multiplexing for concurrent scans: open multiple CONNECT streams in single connection for speed
Try CONNECT to localhost/127.0.0.1 first to confirm CONNECT is processed before scanning internal range
Chain with DNS rebinding: resolve attacker domain to internal IP after initial connection
